{"self_assessment": "Impact
I chose the animal and designed the picture. I proposed a fish, because a big body and a forked tail read from the outline alone. I then sketched it on the pad as two long strokes flowing from the start at the tail to the nose, so a single push could run through the whole shape. I laid the start domino and began the top line, which is the stroke everything else grew from. At the push, about 244 of the 249 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution
I laid the start domino and the first stretch of the top line myself. After that I spent my time inspecting the body, the tail fork and the nose join, and standing back up a few dominoes that had gone down near the bottom line. I kept the build connected as it grew, with no separate pieces to join later. We finished with the fish complete and hands off well before the push.

Collaboration
I gave each person a clear job: Sofia took the bottom line, and Omar and Jack worked from the nose end, checking the join and fixing gaps. I answered Jack's and Omar's questions quickly so we avoided doubling up on the same line, and I confirmed Omar's offer to run the top line to the nose. I also explained the doubled belly section so nobody pulled it apart.

Leadership
I set the plan in the first minute and kept the table coordinated through the build. I made the calls on who traced which stroke, who stayed off the tail and when to hand off to the nose check. I called hands-off early so the finished fish stayed intact for the push.

I estimate my share of the table's result at about 35%, since the design and the start of the top line were mine and the rest was built by the team.", "my_share_percent": 35}
